structs.size_evidence: method 5 (global extent) + alignment: static global netThread @0x14D4AFA68 (lea rcx, netThread in NetStatic::NetStatic@0x140342FFA before the call to NetThread_ctor) ends where the next named global loopback starts, @0x14D4D0030: 0x14D4D0030 - 0x14D4AFA68 = 0x205C8 = 132552. Replay's highest access is the byte at +132549 (NetThread_ctor word store at +132548; NetThread_RecvFrame / NetThread_SendTo byte at +132549/+132548), so the size is at least 132550. The struct starts at an 8-aligned address and holds a vptr, so its size is a multiple of 8: 132552 is the only multiple of 8 in [132550, 132552]. Builder size 132552 agrees. IDA size 1060384 is not supported: nothing in Replay touches +132552 or beyond.

structs.notes: Replay layout: vptr (AsyncRequestProcessor), NetListener 8..32, send ring 32..65872, recv ring 65872..131472, AsyncRequestQueue 131472..132520, then telemetry, socket, started, lastPump, pumpInterval, two bools; size 132552. The first-pass entry (A113) had the send buffer at 40 with 132480 bytes and the tail pads: all three were wrong. The NetThread_vftable has one virtual (slot 0 = NetThread::ProcessRequest, the request handler); the table has no destructor, so no deleting-destructor size is available or needed. NetThread is a static global (no allocation). Dependency for the coordinator: the 24-byte NetListener must be applied before the NetThread layout is written (NetListener's owner).
